title: Anomalies in find/*/items.yml files
description:
Audit of the five `find/*/items.yml` files turned up several issues. The dominant one is a double-slash in URLs (likely from the generators in `make_function_lists/` joining a base URL ending in `/` with a path starting with `/`).

## Summary by file

### `find/tidyclust/items.yml` (5 items)
- All 5 URLs contain `tidymodels.org//reference/...`

### `find/parsnip/items.yml` (197 items)
- 156 URLs with `parsnip.tidymodels.org//reference/...`
- **4 entries with empty `mode: ''` and `package: ''`**:
  - line 199 — `boost_tree` / xgboost
  - line 463 — `linear_reg` / quantreg
  - line 637 — `mlp` / qrnn
  - line 913 — `rand_forest` / grf

### `find/recipes/items.yml` (210 items)
- 116 URLs with `recipes.tidymodels.org//reference/...`

### `find/broom/items.yml` (860 items)
- 393 URLs with double slash (mostly `broom.tidymodels.org//reference/...`, plus 4 `chjackson.github.io/flexsurv//reference/`)
- **68 sparklyr entries all point to bare `https://spark.posit.co/`** with no per-function path (starting line 3041)
- One bare-domain URL: `http://gforge.se` (line 2149, `tidy.rms` / Greg)
- Several `http://` (non-https) URLs (flexsurv, gforge)

### `find/all/items.yml` (2526 items)
- 1392 URLs with `<pkg>.tidymodels.org//reference/...`
- 23 `http://` (non-https) URLs (modelenv, multilevelmod)

## Aggregate

- ~2056 URLs across all files have the `.org//reference/` double-slash pattern.
- 30 URLs use `http://` instead of `https://`.

## Suggested fix

Patch the generators in `make_function_lists/` so base + path joins don't double up the slash, then re-run `Rscript make_function_lists/run_all.R` to regenerate all `items.yml` files. The empty `mode`/`package` rows in parsnip and the bare sparklyr URLs likely need handling in the parsnip/broom generators specifically.

title: Migrate find pages from DT to reactable
description: ## Motivation The current find pages (`find/parsnip/`, `find/recipes/`, `find/broom/`, `find/tidyclust/`) all use the DT (DataTables) package. Several open issues (#238, #31, #6) point to limitations that are either awkward to fix in DT or stem from its age: horizontal overflow, narrow filter dropdowns, and the inability to add clean dropdown filters to HTML-embedded columns. [reactable](https://glin.github.io/reactable/) is a modern R table package built on React Table that addresses all of these more cleanly. ## What reactable gives us - **Column-level dropdown filters** via `colDef(filterInput = "select")` — works correctly for categorical columns regardless of whether the cell content is HTML - **`html = TRUE` per column** — renders HTML cell content without `escape = FALSE` applying globally - **No auto-width expansion** — column widths are stable across filter states (fixes #238) - **Explicit, readable column widths** — easy to set per column, fixing the narrow package dropdown (#31) - **Global search** via `searchable = TRUE` - Cleaner visual output that fits the site's existing typography better than the jQuery UI chrome of DataTables ## Prerequisite: restructure the CSVs The main complication is that the CSVs currently embed HTML directly in `model` and `engine` columns (e.g. `rand_forest`). reactable's filter inputs operate on the underlying cell value, so filtering on an HTML-wrapped string would match `` tags rather than the function name. The fix is to emit separate plain-text columns from the `make_function_lists/` scripts (e.g. `model_label`, `engine_label`) and use those as the filter/factor columns while keeping the HTML versions for display via `colDef(cell = ...)` or `colDef(html = TRUE)`. The `topic` column (already a full `` tag) would keep its current form with `html = TRUE`. ## Scope - Update `make_function_lists/parsnip.R` (and equivalents for other find pages) to emit plain-text label columns alongside the HTML display columns - Replace DT usage in `find/parsnip/index.qmd`, `find/recipes/index.qmd`, `find/broom/index.qmd`, `find/tidyclust/index.qmd`, `find/all/index.qmd` - Add `reactable` to `r-packages:` front matter and `R/installs.R`; remove `DT` and `htmlwidgets` where no longer needed - Update `styles-find.css` as needed (reactable has its own theming via `reactableTheme()`) ## Related - #238 (overflow) — fixed as a side effect - #31 (package column width) — fixed as a side effect - #6 (factor dropdowns) — fixed properly, including for model type

title: update “how to write a step” documentation with sparsity documentation
Note of caution in article on Subsampling for class imbalances
description:
Hello!

Thank you for the amazing work.

I noticed the [Subsampling for class imbalances](https://www.tidymodels.org/learn/models/sub-sampling/) article recommends subsampling to address class imbalances. Please, I would like to suggest adding a warning with a note of caution about the potential deleterious effects of sub-/over-sampling methods. The most recent evidence points to severe harm in calibration and little to no benefit in discrimination. This recent literature does seem somewhat limited to binary classification, though. Happy to make a PR if agreed. Disclaimer: my personal bias comes from the clinical prediction world.

### Recent references on the harms of class imbalance
- [Carriero at al. (2025). The Harms of Class Imbalance Corrections for Machine Learning Based Prediction Models: A Simulation Study. https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.10320](https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.10320)
- [Piccininni at al. (2024). Understanding random resampling techniques for class imbalance correction and their consequences on calibration and discrimination of clinical risk prediction models. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbi.2024.104666](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbi.2024.104666)
### Reference on the equivalence between oversampling and decision threshold selection
[Assunção at al. (2024). Is Augmentation Effective in Improving Prediction in Imbalanced Datasets? https://doi.org/10.6339/24-jds1154](https://doi.org/10.6339/24-JDS1154)


### Text to be removed

In the [Subsampling the data](https://www.tidymodels.org/learn/models/sub-sampling/#subsampling-the-data) section, it is said that:

> "However, subsampling almost always produces models that are better calibrated, meaning that the distributions of the class probabilities are more well behaved. As a result, the default 50% cutoff is much more likely to produce better sensitivity and specificity values than they would otherwise."

I am not sure how this could be the case. For instance, a logistic regression model with sub-/over-sampled data will be poorly calibrated, even with infinite data, due to incorrect intercept. Following [Assunção at al. (2024).](https://doi.org/10.6339/24-JDS1154), setting the probability cutoff to the outcome prevalence seems to suffice, without harming calibration. Perhaps warning about the difference between a class imbalance problem and a sample size problem may be beneficial.

Thanks again,
Giuliano

title: Suggest updating documentation to use base R pipe |> instead of %>%
description:
Hello team, 

I'd like to suggest updating examples in the tidymodels documentation to use the native R pipe operator `|>` instead of `%>%`.

Since R 4.1.0, the base pipe has become widely adopted in the R community, and many modern tutorials and packages are gradually transitioning to it. 

Current style:

```r
linear_reg() %>% 
  set_engine("keras")
#> Linear Regression Model Specification (regression)
#> 
#> Computational engine: keras
```

Suggested style:

```r
linear_reg() |>
  set_engine("keras")
#> Linear Regression Model Specification (regression)
#> 
#> Computational engine: keras
```

Thank you for your work on tidymodels!

title: Add 11 missing articles to left-hand sidebar navigation
description:
## Summary

11 articles exist in the repository but are not accessible via the left-hand sidebar navigation in `_quarto.yml`.

## Missing Articles

### Statistics Section (3)
- `/learn/statistics/survival-case-study/` - Comprehensive survival analysis
- `/learn/statistics/survival-metrics/` - Dynamic performance metrics
- `/learn/statistics/survival-metrics-details/` - IPCW and advanced metrics

### Models Section (3)
- `/learn/models/bootstrap-metrics/` - Bootstrap confidence intervals
- `/learn/models/calibration/` - Model calibration methods
- `/learn/models/parsnip-predictions/` - Comprehensive prediction reference

### Develop Section (1)
- `/learn/develop/filtro/` - Creating score class objects with S7

### Work Section (4)
- `/learn/work/fairness-detectors/` - GPT detector fairness case study
- `/learn/work/fairness-readmission/` - Hospital readmission fairness
- `/learn/work/sparse-matrix/` - Tuning with sparse matrices
- `/learn/work/sparse-recipe/` - Creating sparse data with recipes

## Proposed Fix

Replace explicit file listings in `_quarto.yml` with Quarto's glob pattern auto-discovery:

```yaml
- section: "Perform Statistical Analyses"
  contents: learn/statistics/*/index.qmd
```

This would automatically include all articles and prevent future navigation gaps.

 23.     │ └─base::withCallingHandlers(...)
 24.     ├─purrr:::call_with_cleanup(...)

Here's the full code in the example 

```
library(tidymodels)  
library(modeldata)  
library(mda)  

set_new_model("discrim_mixture")
set_model_mode(model = "discrim_mixture", mode = "classification")
set_model_engine(
  "discrim_mixture", 
  mode = "classification", 
  eng = "mda"
)

set_dependency("discrim_mixture", eng = "mda", pkg = "mda")

set_model_arg(
  model = "discrim_mixture",
  eng = "mda",
  parsnip = "sub_classes",
  original = "subclasses",
  func = list(pkg = "foo", fun = "bar"),
  has_submodel = FALSE
)

discrim_mixture <-
  function(mode = "classification",  sub_classes = NULL) { 
    if (mode  != "classification") { 
      rlang::abort("`mode` should be 'classification'.")
    }
    
    args <- list(sub_classes = rlang::enquo(sub_classes))
    
    new_model_spec(
      "discrim_mixture",
      args = args, # Argument names (`sub_classes`) should be defaulted to NULL  
      eng_args = NULL, 
      mode = mode,
      method = NULL,
      engine = NULL
    )
  }

set_fit(
  model = "discrim_mixture",
  eng = "mda",
  mode = "classification",
  value = list(
    interface = "formula",
    protect = c("formula", "data"),
    func = c(pkg = "mda", fun = "mda"),
    defaults = list()
  )
)

set_encoding(
  model = "discrim_mixture",
  eng = "mda",
  mode = "classification",
  options = list(
    predictor_indicators = "traditional",
    compute_intercept = TRUE,
    remove_intercept = TRUE,
    allow_sparse_x = FALSE
  )
)

class_info <- 
  list(
    pre = NULL, 
    post = NULL, 
    func = c(fun = "predict"), 
    args =
      list(
        object = rlang::expr(object$fit),
        newdata = rlang::expr(new_data),
        type = "class"
      )
  )

set_pred(
  model = "discrim_mixture",
  eng = "mda",
  mode = "classification",
  type = "class",
  value = class_info
)

prob_info <-
  pred_value_template(
    post = function(x, object) {
      tibble::as_tibble(x)
    },
    func = c(fun = "predict"),
    object = rlang::expr(object$fit),
    newdata = rlang::expr(new_data),
    type = "posterior"
  )

set_pred(
  model = "discrim_mixture",
  eng = "mda",
  mode = "classification",
  type = "prob",
  value = prob_info
)

data("two_class_dat", package = "modeldata")
set.seed(4622)

example_split <- initial_split(two_class_dat, prop = 0.99)
example_train <- training(example_split)
example_test  <-  testing(example_split)

mda_spec <- discrim_mixture(sub_classes = 2) %>% 
  set_engine("mda")

mda_fit <- mda_spec %>%
  fit(Class ~ ., data = example_train)

# Predict Class without Probabilities 
predict(mda_fit, new_data = example_test) %>% 
  bind_cols(example_test %>% select(Class))

# Predict Class with Probabilities 
predict(mda_fit, new_data = example_test, type = "prob") %>%
  bind_cols(example_test %>% select(Class))

sub_classes <- function(range = c(1L, 10L),
                        trans = NULL) {
  new_quant_param(
    type = "integer",
    range = range,
    inclusive = c(TRUE, TRUE),
    trans = trans,
    label = c(sub_classes = "# Sub-Classes"),
    finalize = NULL
  )
}

mda_spec <- 
  discrim_mixture(sub_classes = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("mda")

set.seed(452)

cv <- vfold_cv(example_train)

mda_tune_res <- mda_spec %>% 
  tune_grid(Class ~ ., cv, grid = 4)  

rlang::last_trace()
```

title: Only install packages needed for affected pages in selective re-render CI
description:
In the \`check-cran-releases.yml\` workflow, the \`rerender\` job currently runs \`installs.R\` which installs all packages for the entire site, regardless of which pages are actually being re-rendered.

Since we now have \`package_map.json\` mapping packages to the pages that depend on them, we could instead:

1. Determine which pages will be re-rendered (union of pages affected by updated packages)
2. Look up which packages those pages need from \`package_map.json\`
3. Install only that subset of packages

This would reduce CI time significantly when only a small number of pages need re-rendering (e.g. a single package update that affects 2-3 pages).

The main complexity is handling the install correctly — some packages in \`installs.R\` have special setup steps (torch, keras, catboost) that may or may not be needed depending on which pages are affected.

title: Formula for time-dependent Brier score on https://www.tidymodels.org/learn/statistics/survival-metrics/
description: The formula for the time-dependent Brier score on https://www.tidymodels.org/learn/statistics/survival-metrics/ appears to be written incorrectly. In the block for non-events, $y_{it}$ should be replaced by the indicator for a non-event; i.e.,  $1 - y_{it}$. (If this weren't done the numerator for both events and non-events would be the same.) Second, the sum should be divided by $n$ = the number of individuals with non-missing survival data (including censored entries) instead of $W_t$. These are in line with the Graf, 1999 articles and what seems to be coded at https://github.com/tidymodels/yardstick/blob/main/R/surv-brier_survival.R .

title: A possible error in "Create your own recipe step function"?
description:
From [website](https://www.tidymodels.org/learn/develop/recipes/): In `step_percentile()`, `terms = terms` is passed on to `step_percentile_new()`. This will set `terms` member of the step to function `stats::terms`. However, in `prep.step_percentile()`, `x$terms` is used in `recipes_eval_select()` as the first argument, which is expected to be a quosure list to select variables to apply the step. Since `x$term = stats::terms` is a function, this will throw an error:
```
Error in enexpr(expr) : 
  Can't splice an object of type `closure` because it is not a vector
```
I changed the function call to `step_percentile_new()` to follows (note the change `terms = rlang::enquos(...)`, and it worked as expected:
```
step_percentile_new(
      terms = rlang::enquos(...), 
      trained = trained,
      role = role, 
      ref_dist = ref_dist,
      options = options,
      skip = skip,
      id = id
)
```
